findings.title: Feed content is double-unescaped and stored as raw HTML, giving stored XSS on the forum
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` decodes entities that SimpleRSS has already decoded from the XML, so text meant to be shown literally (for example `&lt;img onerror=...&gt;` in the feed) becomes live markup. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates the post with `cook_method: raw_html` (topic_embed.rb:22). `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb:133), which skips the Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` unescaped (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), and the same cooked HTML appears in the forum topic. A feed item containing a script or event-handler payload therefore runs on the forum origin for every visitor, including staff. Feed content is third-party data, so this crosses a trust boundary. Run imported content through the normal sanitizer before storing raw HTML, and remove the extra unescape.

findings.title: Dangling `if` modifier in `<%- end if %>` makes the embed template invalid
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` closes the `if` opened on line 2 but leaves a stray `if` modifier with no condition. Once ERB compiles this, the result is not valid Ruby (the modifier is followed by the compiler's statement separator), so the `best` template fails whenever it is rendered. The intent is clearly `<%- end %>`. This breaks the main embed page for every request that finds an existing topic. The controller specs do not catch it because they never render views (no `render_views`), so a view or request spec is needed.

findings.title: PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an outer transaction that has not committed
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator#create` calls `enqueue_jobs` (which triggers `process_post` and `feature_topic_users`) before the outer transaction commits. PostCreator's own comment says jobs must be enqueued after the transaction because workers may start on uncommitted data. With Sidekiq, a `process_post` job can run before the post and the TopicEmbed row are visible, find nothing, or fail, so the post is never processed (oneboxes, image sizes, and so on). Enqueue after the outermost commit, or do not wrap the creator in an outer transaction.

findings.title: Anonymous requests can force unlimited outbound fetches and full feed polls
findings.body: For any unknown `embed_url`, each request enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job without checking the host (the controller only checks the referer). The only throttle is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` in topic_retriever.rb:26-28, which runs inside the worker and is keyed on the exact URL string. An attacker can vary a query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key causes an outbound HTTP fetch of the embeddable host, and when feed polling is enabled it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (topic_retriever.rb:41), which downloads and re-imports the entire feed. Nothing rate-limits the endpoint, so this is a cheap way to exhaust outbound bandwidth and Sidekiq capacity. Validate the host in the controller before enqueueing, throttle per normalized URL in the request path, and do not run a full feed poll from a request-driven job.

findings.title: `force: true` on a new table migration drops any existing topic_embeds table
findings.body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops an existing `topic_embeds` table before creating it. A migration that creates a new table gains nothing from this option and makes it destructive: running it in an environment where the table already exists (a partially migrated database, or another branch that created the table) silently deletes every embed-to-topic mapping. The importer depends on those mappings to avoid duplicate topics. Remove `force: true`.

findings.title: Unrelated migration gains `force: true`, which drops existing top_topics data if rerun
findings.body: This change adds `force: true` to the `top_topics` table creation. It is unrelated to embedding. If the migration runs in an environment where `top_topics` already exists with data, the table and all its counters are dropped. If the schema needs changing, add a new migration instead of editing one that may already have run.

findings.title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll, and nil content raises NoMethodError
findings.body: The `rss.items.each` loop has no per-item error handling. `i.content` can be nil for feed items that only supply a description, so `i.content.scrub` on line 35 raises NoMethodError. `i.title` can also be nil. `TopicEmbed.import` can raise too, for example when the URL exceeds 255 characters, or when the embed's post has been deleted. Any of these aborts the loop, and the job has `retry: false`, so nothing retries. The next hourly run reaches the same item and fails again, so every item after it is never imported. Guard nil content and title, and rescue and log errors per item.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring matching, so a prefix origin is accepted
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison. Any sender whose origin is a prefix of the forum URL passes. With `discourseUrl = "https://community.example.com/"`, a page served from the registrable domain `https://community.example.co` has an origin that is a prefix, so `indexOf` returns 0 and the message is accepted. The handler also never checks `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`. The practical effect is that a lookalike site can resize the iframe, but the check is wrong. Compare the exact origin (scheme, host, port) of `discourseUrl` with `e.origin`.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options 'ALLOWALL' is not a valid value and is ignored by browsers
findings.body: Valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unknown values, so this header does nothing; framing is permitted only because the browser ignores it. It also overwrites any X-Frame-Options set earlier in the request. If the intent is to allow framing from the configured host, use `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` with the embeddable host and remove this header.

findings.title: setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a throttle key with no TTL
findings.body: `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire` are two separate commands. If the process dies or the connection drops between them, `retrieved:<url>` persists with no TTL. Non-staff users are then permanently throttled for that URL and it is never retried. Use one atomic command, `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

findings.title: Missing post for an existing embed causes NoMethodError on update
findings.body: `post = embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. When the content hash differs, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`. The stale embed row is never repaired, and in PollFeed this exception aborts the whole loop (poll_feed.rb:31), so every later item is skipped. Handle a missing post explicitly, for example by recreating the post or removing the stale embed.

findings.title: Readability attribute whitelist does not restrict URL schemes
findings.body: `attributes: %w[href src]` limits which attribute names survive, but it does not check URL schemes. A `<a href="javascript:...">` from the fetched page can survive into the body. That body is stored as raw_html (cook_method), so the link runs script on the forum when clicked. The source is the configured embeddable host, so exploiting this needs that site to be compromised or malicious, but the forum should not accept unsanitized HTML from it. Pass the output through the normal sanitizer with an allowed-scheme list.

findings.title: Imported-from footer interpolates the URL into HTML without escaping
findings.body: The footer is built as `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The URL comes from the feed link or id and is inserted unescaped into a body stored as raw HTML. A link such as `http://x.test/'>` injects markup. The URL check on line 11 uses `^`, which matches after any newline, so the scheme check is also weaker than intended. Escape the URL before interpolating it, and anchor the scheme check at the start of the string.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) with no length check, so long URLs fail at insert
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` creates varchar(255) in PostgreSQL. The value comes from unauthenticated request params (embed_controller.rb:9) and from feed links, and nothing checks its length. A longer URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise StatementInvalid after the page has been fetched and the post built. The transaction rolls back, and every retry fails the same way. Validate the length at the controller and model, or use a text column.

findings.title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the entire posts table
findings.body: On PostgreSQL releases before 11, `add_column` with a default and `null: false` rewrites the whole posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum, reads and writes to posts are blocked for the duration. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL constraint, or schedule the downtime explicitly.

findings.title: The --category option is silently removed from the Disqus import CLI
findings.body: Removing `method_option :category` means `thor disqus:import --category X` now fails with an unknown-option error, and imported topics no longer get a category. This is a breaking change to the command-line interface that the PR description does not mention. Restore the option or document the removal.

findings.title: Disqus import now fetches every thread live with no error handling and duplicates comments on re-run
findings.body: Replacing PostCreator with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` makes the import fetch each thread's live URL with `open(url).read`. There is no timeout, no rescue, and no per-thread handling, so one 404 or network error aborts the import midway. The `ensure` block restores settings, but earlier threads are already imported. Re-running the import also appends every comment again: `import` returns the existing post, and the loop keeps creating posts for it. Rescue per thread, and skip comment creation when the topic already existed.

findings.title: New gems are added for both Rails modes, but only the Rails 4 lockfile is updated
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally, and Rails 3 mode uses the same Gemfile with the default `Gemfile.lock`. Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this PR. In Rails 3 mode, `bundle install --deployment` or `--frozen` will fail because the lockfile is missing these gems. Update the Rails 3 lockfile too, or gate the gems by mode.

findings.title: Test named 'is 404' asserts only failure, and no test renders the view
findings.body: The example is titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' but only checks `should_not be_success`. It passes because the `ensure_embeddable` filter raises first when embeddable_host is unset, so `params.require` is never exercised. No spec renders the `best` or `loading` templates (no `render_views`), so a broken template like the one in best.html.erb:6 goes undetected. Add a request spec that checks the status code and renders the templates.

findings.title: Every TopicRetriever example stubs the method under test, leaving the throttle and feed logic untested
findings.body: Each example in the 'with a valid host' context stubs `retrieved_recently?` or `perform_retrieve`. The Redis throttle, the feed-first branch in `perform_retrieve` (topic_retriever.rb:40-43), the existing-embed early return, and `fetch_http` are never exercised. The most important behavior, that a second request within 60 seconds does not fetch again, has no coverage. Add examples that use a real or mock Redis and exercise `perform_retrieve` directly.

findings.title: PollFeed import logic has no test coverage, only the gating conditions
findings.body: The spec only checks when `poll_feed` is called and stubs `poll_feed` in the delegation example. The actual import path, including URL filtering, nil title or content handling, the `TopicEmbed.import` call per item, and the error behavior, is untested. That is the riskiest code in the feature (see the XSS and per-item abort findings above). Add examples that feed a sample RSS document through `poll_feed`.

findings.title: Kernel#open is used on an admin-supplied URL
findings.body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open. In Ruby 2.x, a string beginning with `|` is executed as a shell command rather than fetched. The setting is admin-only, so the exposure is limited, but the call should be explicit. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (open-uri) so only HTTP(S) fetches are possible.

findings.title: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1 or later
findings.body: `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1. If this application still targets Ruby 2.0 (as Discourse did in late 2013), every poll that reaches this line raises NoMethodError. Confirm the supported Ruby version, or use an encoding-safe alternative.

findings.title: cook_method is accepted from any opts hash and can bypass sanitization
findings.body: `setup_post` now copies `opts[:cook_method]` onto the post. Setting it to raw_html stores the body unsanitized, because `Post#cook` returns raw HTML directly. If any controller forwards request parameters into PostCreator, an API or web user could create raw_html posts. Check that user-facing controllers whitelist their params and never pass `cook_method`, or only honor it from trusted server-side callers.

findings.title: Documented options list omits the new cook_method option
findings.body: The header comment lists the accepted PostCreator options, but `cook_method`, which this PR adds and which changes how the body is rendered and sanitized, is not documented. Add it, with its accepted values and the fact that raw_html skips the sanitizer.
